title: Rigveda 5.58: To the Maruts
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.58: To the Maruts: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.58 is a hymn of 8 verses addressed to the Maruts. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 377v-378v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.58.1 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 3, varga 23); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 377v
translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>tam u̍ nū̱naṁ tavi̍ṣīmantam eṣāṁ stu̱ṣe ga̱ṇam māru̍ta̱ṁ navya̍sīnām | ya ā̱śva̍śvā̱ ama̍va̱d vaha̍nta u̱teśi̍re a̱mṛta̍sya sva̱rāja̍ḥ ||
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>Now do I glorify their mighty cohort, the company of these the youthful Maruts, Who ride impetuous on with rapid horses, and radiant in themselves, are Lords of Amrit.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 377v (numbered 50v by the scribe) (OPenn image 378, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.57.6 ‹-āyudhā ratheṣu vaḥ viśvā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 378r (numbered 51r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.58.2 ‹-amitāḥ mahi-tvā vandasva vipra›. Verse 5.58.1 ends on this page.
translation.edition_text: <sup>1</sup>tam | oṃ iti | nūnam | taviṣī-mantam | eṣām | stuṣe | gaṇam | mārutam | navyasīnām | ye | āśu-aśvāḥ | ama-vat | vahante | uta | īśire | amṛtasya | sva-rājaḥ

translation.original_ref: RV 5.58.2-5 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 3, varga 23); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 378r
translation.original_text:
2tve̱ṣaṁ ga̱ṇaṁ ta̱vasa̱ṁ khādi̍hasta̱ṁ dhuni̍vratam mā̱yina̱ṁ dāti̍vāram | ma̱yo̱bhuvo̱ ye ami̍tā mahi̱tvā vanda̍sva vipra tuvi̱rādha̍so̱ nṝn ||
3ā vo̍ yantūdavā̱hāso̍ a̱dya vṛ̱ṣṭiṁ ye viśve̍ ma̱ruto̍ ju̱nanti̍ | a̱yaṁ yo a̱gnir ma̍ruta̱ḥ sami̍ddha e̱taṁ ju̍ṣadhvaṁ kavayo yuvānaḥ ||
4yū̱yaṁ rājā̍na̱m irya̱ṁ janā̍ya vibhvata̱ṣṭaṁ ja̍nayathā yajatrāḥ | yu̱ṣmad e̍ti muṣṭi̱hā bā̱hujū̍to yu̱ṣmat sada̍śvo marutaḥ su̱vīra̍ḥ ||
5a̱rā i̱ved aca̍ramā̱ ahe̍va̱ pra-pra̍ jāyante̱ aka̍vā̱ maho̍bhiḥ | pṛśne̍ḥ pu̱trā u̍pa̱māso̱ rabhi̍ṣṭhā̱ḥ svayā̍ ma̱tyā ma̱ruta̱ḥ sam mi̍mikṣuḥ ||
translation.text:
2The mighty glittering band, arm-bound with bracelets, givers of bliss, unmeasured in their greatness, With magical powers, bountiful, ever-roaring,– these, liberal Heroes, venerate thou singer.
3This day may all your water-bringers, Maruts, they who impel the falling rain, approach us. This fire, O Maruts, hath been duly kindled; let it find favour with you, youthful Sages.
4Ye raise up for the folk an active ruler whom, Holy Ones! a Master's hand hath fashioned. Ye send the fighter hand to hand, armmighty, and the brave hero, Maruts with good horses.
5They spring forth more and more, strong in their glories, like days, like spokes where none are last in order. Highest and mightiest are the Sons of Pr̥iṣni. Firm to their own intention cling the Maruts.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 378r (numbered 51r by the scribe) (OPenn image 378, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.58.2 ‹-amitāḥ mahi-tvā vandasva vipra›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 378v (numbered 51v by the scribe), begins in RV 5.58.6 ‹kṣodante āpaḥ riṇate vanāni›. Verses 5.58.2-5 end on this page; 5.58.2 begins on fol. 377v (numbered 50v by the scribe).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.58.6-8 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 3, varga 23); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 378v
translation.original_text:
6yat prāyā̍siṣṭa̱ pṛṣa̍tībhi̱r aśvai̍r vīḻupa̱vibhi̍r maruto̱ rathe̍bhiḥ | kṣoda̍nta̱ āpo̍ riṇa̱te vanā̱ny avo̱sriyo̍ vṛṣa̱bhaḥ kra̍ndatu̱ dyauḥ ||
7prathi̍ṣṭa̱ yāma̍n pṛthi̱vī ci̍d eṣā̱m bharte̍va̱ garbha̱ṁ svam ic chavo̍ dhuḥ | vātā̱n hy aśvā̍n dhu̱ry ā̍yuyu̱jre va̱rṣaṁ sveda̍ṁ cakrire ru̱driyā̍saḥ ||
8ha̱ye naro̱ maru̍to mṛ̱ḻatā̍ na̱s tuvī̍maghāso̱ amṛ̍tā̱ ṛta̍jñāḥ | satya̍śruta̱ḥ kava̍yo̱ yuvā̍no̱ bṛha̍dgirayo bṛ̱had u̱kṣamā̍ṇāḥ ||
translation.text:
6When ye have hastened on with spotted coursers, O Maruts, on your cars with strong-wrought fellies, The waters are disturbed, the woods are shattered. Let Dyaus the Red Steer send his thunder downward.
7Even Earth hath spread herself wide at their coming, and they as husbands have with power impregned her. They to the pole have yoked the winds for coursers: their sweat have they made rain, these Sons of Rudra.
8Ho! Maruts, Heroes, skilled in Law, immortal, be gracious unto us, ye rich in treasures, Ye hearers of the truth, ye sage and youthful, grown mighty, dwelling on the lofty mountains.

The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 379r (numbered 52r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.59.3 ‹-uttamam sūryaḥ na cakṣuḥ›. Verses 5.58.6-8 end on this page; 5.58.6 begins on fol. 378r (numbered 51r by the scribe).
